answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce deposit and earn reputation through signed transactions with peers. A prism of random audits tests linked tasks; identities that collude, duplicate answers, or contradict their history lose deposit and reputation. A Sybil campaign therefore pays the deposit for every fake identity and risks correlated slashing: scaling the attack raises its cost linearly, while the ocean of honest interactions makes a nebula of fresh aliases difficult to seed.
